name: Min XOR pairs
html:
Hey coder. We are going to start with a new question of Bit manipulation in this article.

We first want you to go through the outline of the problem to understand it better.

You are given an array of distinct integers and have to print all pairs of integers in the array whose XOR value is minimum.


Important Links : Problem Link, Solution Video


BRUTE FORCE APPROACH

Reader, the brute force approach would be to generate all pairs with two nested loops so we get the number of pairs equals nC2 and for every pair, we can calculate the XOR result and then return the minimum result.

Say, the array given to us is [a,b,c,d,e].

The number of pairs for this array are nC2=5C2=10 as shown in figure 1.

But, this approach has a time complexity of O(n2) because of the nested loops.

Let's see if we can optimize it.

OPTIMIZED APPROACH

We can optimize the solution for an array [a,b,c] by using sorting.

  • CLAIM:
    If a <= b <= c then, either a ^ b < a ^ c or b ^ c < a ^ c
  • PROOF:
    1. a = 1 1 0 1 0 ... => [same bits i.e. 1101] [different bit i.e. 0] [non-significant bits]
      b = 1 1 0 1 0 ... => [same bits i.e. 1101] [0] [non-significant bits]
      c =1 1 0 1 1 ... => [same bits i.e. 1101] [different bit i.e. 1] [non-significant bits]
      a^b = 0 0 0 0 1 ... => [0000] [1] [redundant]
      a^c = 0 0 0 0 0 ... => [0000] [0] [redundant]
      Here a^b < a^c
    2. a = 1 1 0 1 0 ... => [same bits i.e. 1101] [different bit i.e. 0] [non-significant bits]
      b = 1 1 0 1 1 ... => [same bits i.e. 1101] [1] [non-significant bits]
      c = 1 1 0 1 1 ... => [same bits i.e. 1101] [different bit i.e. 1] [non-significant bits]
      b^ c = 0 0 0 0 1 ... => [0000] [1] [redundant]
      a^c = 0 0 0 0 0 ... => [0000] [0] [redundant]
      Here b^c < a^c
    Hence proved.

This claim implies that XOR of non-adjacent sorted numbers will always be less than XOR of the adjacent sorted number, i.e., if we have numbers [a, b, c] we already know that either pair (a, b) or pair (b, c) will be our result so pair (a, c) will be redundant.

Expanding this idea to numbers [ a, b, c, d, e] then we only need to check XORs of (a, b), (b, c), (c, d), and (d, e).

Hence after sorting which takes O(NlogN) time we only need to traverse the array once to get our adjacent pairs XOR values.

CODE

Reader, we hope you have understood the above optimized approach. Give coding this problem a fair try. If you get stuck somewhere, you can always refer to the code given below.

import java.io.*; import java.util.*; public class Main { public static void solution(int[] arr) { Arrays.sort(arr); ArrayList< String> res=new ArrayList< >(); int min=Integer.MAX_VALUE; for(int i=0;i< arr.length-1;i++){ int xor=arr[i] ^ arr[i+1]; if(xor< min){ min=xor; res=new ArrayList< >(); res.add(arr[i]+", "+arr[i+1]); }else if(xor==min){ res.add(arr[i]+", "+arr[i+1]); } } for(String val: res){ System.out.println(val); } } public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); int n = scn.nextInt(); int[] arr = new int[n]; for(int i = 0 ; i < n; i++){ arr[i] = scn.nextInt(); } solution(arr); } }
java; true"; Analysis Time Complexity:

O(nlogn+n)

Here nlogn time is taken for sorting of the array and n time is taken to check the minimum XOR pair.

Space Complexity:

O(1)


We conclude our discussion here. If you have any doubts in this article, we highly suggest you watch its solution video.
